semantic_correction.stem: A hospital is designing a transition-of-care program for clients discharged after a heart-failure hospitalization. Which component best aligns with current AHA/ACC/HFSA guidance?

options.A: Provide comprehensive discharge teaching, arrange timely follow-up, and communicate the transition plan clearly to outpatient clinicians.
options.B: Limit discharge teaching to the medication list and defer weight and symptom-response education until a later visit.
options.C: Avoid early follow-up because contact soon after discharge has no role in heart-failure continuity of care.
options.D: Use the transition program as a replacement for ongoing outpatient heart-failure management after discharge.

semantic_correction.rationale: The AHA/ACC/HFSA heart-failure guideline identifies the transition from inpatient to outpatient care as a vulnerable period and recommends comprehensive discharge planning. Written discharge material should address activity, diet, medications, follow-up appointments, weight monitoring, cardiac rehabilitation, and what to do if symptoms worsen. The hospital course and transitional plan should be transmitted clearly and promptly to clinicians providing follow-up care. The guideline also describes early outpatient follow-up as a central element of transitional care. Therefore option A best reflects recommended continuity-of-care practices.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Plan heart-failure transitions using comprehensive discharge education, timely follow-up, and clear communication with outpatient clinicians.

audit_findings_append.finding: The original answer was uniquely longest. The revised item directly tests the central transition-of-care elements without overloading the correct choice.

option_audit.A: Correct. It matches the guideline's discharge education, follow-up, and outpatient communication recommendations.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Weight monitoring and symptom-response teaching are part of the recommended discharge material.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Early outpatient follow-up is explicitly described as a central element of transitional care.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Transitional care coordinates ongoing management; it does not replace longitudinal outpatient care.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone combines the core evidence-based transition components described in the guideline.
cueing_check: All four choices are transition-program components of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
